title: Why text needs to be numbered

cues.en: Well, the answer to the question of the title is actually pretty straightforward.
cues.zh: 其實，標題這個問題的答案很直接。

cues.en: Text needs to be transformed into numbers because deep learning models are based on processing numbers.
cues.zh: 文字需要轉成數字，因為深度學習模型處理的是數字。

cues.en: But I'm also going to cover several other related topics in this video, including introducing you to
cues.zh: 不過，這支影片也會談幾個相關主題，包括介紹

cues.en: some terminology and also introducing you to some concepts in tokenization and embeddings that make
cues.zh: 一些術語，以及斷詞和嵌入的概念。這些問題讓

cues.en: language processing already pretty complicated and challenging, even before the data actually get into the language model like GPT.
cues.zh: 語言處理在資料進入 GPT 這類語言模型之前，就已相當複雜、充滿挑戰。

cues.en: So just a heads up, there are several concepts that I will introduce and claims that I will make in
cues.zh: 先提醒各位，這裡介紹的幾個概念與提出的論點，

cues.en: this video that I will go into much more detail about in later videos, also with lots of code demonstrations.
cues.zh: 我會在後面的影片中更詳細說明，並提供許多程式示範。

cues.en: So if you find some of the things I say here in this video to be interesting but not fully developed,
cues.zh: 所以，如果你覺得這裡有些說法很有意思，卻還沒有充分展開，

cues.en: then don't worry, I'm going to get into more detail throughout this and the next several sections.
cues.zh: 別擔心，這一章和接下來幾章都會更深入探討。

cues.en: So yeah, language models are basically just simple mathematical operations that act on numbers.
cues.zh: 語言模型基本上就是對數字進行簡單的數學運算。

cues.en: And then you put billions or trillions of these simple calculations together.
cues.zh: 再把數十億、數兆次這樣的簡單計算組合起來，

cues.en: And the result is pretty sophisticated and really complex.
cues.zh: 結果就會相當精巧，也非常複雜。

cues.en: But still, at the end of the day, language models are based on mathematics.
cues.zh: 但說到底，語言模型仍以數學為基礎。

cues.en: And of course, math is based on numbers.
cues.zh: 而數學當然以數字為基礎。

cues.en: Now, if you have studied the philosophy of math then you might disagree with this claim.
cues.zh: 如果你研究過數學哲學，可能會不同意這個說法。

cues.en: You might say that actually math is based on axioms, structures, and propositions that are not necessarily numeric.
cues.zh: 你可能會說，數學其實以公理、結構與命題為基礎，而不一定涉及數字。

cues.en: Now that is true, but practically speaking, and certainly when it comes to deep learning, all the
cues.zh: 這沒錯，但就實務而言，尤其在深度學習裡，

cues.en: math that is used in these kinds of applications is based on processing numbers on digital computers,
cues.zh: 這些應用使用的數學，都是在數位電腦上處理數字，

cues.en: things like optimization algorithms that we use, and probabilities for selecting tokens or categorizing texts are all based on numbers.
cues.zh: 例如我們採用的最佳化演算法，以及選擇 token 或分類文字的機率，都以數字為基礎。

cues.en: So therefore the text must be transformed into numbers in order to be processed in a deep learning model.
cues.zh: 因此，文字必須先轉成數字，才能交由深度學習模型處理。

cues.en: Now let me start introducing you to some terms.
cues.zh: 先來介紹一些術語。

cues.en: The first term is token.
cues.zh: 第一個是 token，詞元。

cues.en: In the context of natural language processing, a token is a piece of text that can be represented by a number, and not just any type of number.
cues.zh: 在自然語言處理中，token 是一段可以用數字表示的文字，而且不是任意類型的數字。

cues.en: I'm specifically referring to integers or whole numbers like zero or 1 or 10,000 and so on.
cues.zh: 這裡特別指整數，例如 0、1、10,000 等等。

cues.en: And what is that piece of text are we talking about a letter or a word or a sentence?
cues.zh: 那麼，這段文字是指字母、單字，還是句子？

cues.en: Maybe a whole paragraph?
cues.zh: 也可能是一整段嗎？

cues.en: Well, tokens can be many different sizes of text.
cues.zh: token 所涵蓋的文字長度可以有很多種。

cues.en: For example, we have character tokens.
cues.zh: 例如，字元 token。

cues.en: So the word hello is made up of five letters which would correspond to four tokens.
cues.zh: hello 這個字有五個字母，對應到四個 token。

cues.en: Now these are the actual tokens that the GPT tokenizer uses.
cues.zh: 這些是 GPT tokenizer 實際使用的 token。

cues.en: So I'm not just making up these numbers arbitrarily.
cues.zh: 所以，這些數字並不是我隨意編的。

cues.en: These are actually used in real applications in GPT models like ChatGPT.
cues.zh: 它們確實用在 ChatGPT 這類 GPT 模型的實際應用中。

cues.en: So this is one example where every letter or character has its own integer.
cues.zh: 這個例子裡，每個字母或字元都有自己的整數編號。

cues.en: We can also tokenize based on a subword.
cues.zh: 我們也可以以子詞為單位斷詞。

cues.en: A subword is a little piece of a word.
cues.zh: 子詞就是單字的一小部分。

cues.en: Sometimes subwords are also correspond to words on their own, and sometimes they are parts of words that couldn't exist on their own.
cues.zh: 有些子詞本身也是單字，有些則是無法獨立存在的單字片段。

cues.en: So in this example, we can break up the word hello into two subwords he and lo.
cues.zh: 這個例子把 hello 拆成 he 和 lo 兩個子詞。

cues.en: And these are the token subword IDs for these two subwords.
cues.zh: 這些就是兩個子詞的 token ID。

cues.en: And then we can have an entire word already being a token.
cues.zh: 也可以用一整個單字作為一個 token。

cues.en: So from these examples, you can see that there is a variety of ways of breaking up a word or text into tokens.
cues.zh: 從這些例子可以看出，把單字或文字拆成 token 的方法有很多。

cues.en: And you know, it's not that we have to pick one of these schemes.
cues.zh: 而且，我們不必只選其中一種方式。

cues.en: In fact, all of these tokens are perfectly valid on Gpts tokenizer.
cues.zh: 事實上，這些 token 在 GPT 的 tokenizer 中都有效。

cues.en: So a bit more about terminology.
cues.zh: 再補充一點術語。

cues.en: The term token refers to a piece of text.
cues.zh: token 指的是一段文字。

cues.en: So a string like the word hello, or a subword or an individual character that's a token.
cues.zh: 例如 hello 這樣的字串、子詞，或單一字元，都是 token。

cues.en: And the integer or the whole number that is associated with each token is called a token id or token index.
cues.zh: 與每個 token 對應的整數，稱為 token ID 或 token 索引。

cues.en: You might also come across other words like a vocab index or a token number, something like that.
cues.zh: 你也可能看到詞彙表索引、token 編號之類的其他說法。

cues.en: But these are the two most common terms token ID or token index.
cues.zh: 但最常見的是 token ID 與 token 索引。

cues.en: But why do we even need to use subwords or whole words as tokens?
cues.zh: 可是，為什麼還需要以子詞或整個單字當作 token？

cues.en: Doesn't that just create a huge amount of unnecessary tokens?
cues.zh: 這樣不是會產生大量不必要的 token 嗎？

cues.en: Because there are so many words across so many languages that we we might want a language model to be able to understand.
cues.zh: 畢竟，我們可能希望語言模型理解許多語言，而各種語言都有那麼多單字。

cues.en: So why don't we just use all the elementary characters as tokens?
cues.zh: 為什麼不直接以所有基本字元作為 token？

cues.en: In fact, we can.
cues.zh: 其實可以。

cues.en: And it's not necessarily a terrible idea, but it is a little bit tricky.
cues.zh: 這也不一定是個壞主意，只是有些棘手。

cues.en: A purely character based tokenization would look something like this, where we have numbers assigned to each letter.
cues.zh: 純字元斷詞大致會像這樣：替每個字母指定一個數字。

cues.en: Then we need more tokens.
cues.zh: 接著還需要更多 token。

cues.en: Numbers.
cues.zh: 還有數字。

cues.en: So more integers for the numbers.
cues.zh: 所以，也要替數字指定整數編號。

cues.en: And of course we have punctuations.
cues.zh: 當然，還有標點符號，

cues.en: and like these weird kinds of characters and so on.
cues.zh: 以及這些特殊字元等等。

cues.en: Of course, this is just in English, so we'd also need numbers for Chinese characters and Arabic characters and Hebrew characters and so on.
cues.zh: 而這還只是英文，因此也需要為中文字、阿拉伯文字、希伯來文字等指定編號。

cues.en: And how about things like emojis and currency symbols and on and on and on.
cues.zh: 那表情符號、貨幣符號，以及其他各種符號呢？

cues.en: So it turns out that there are several limitations of using only characters as tokens.
cues.zh: 所以，僅以字元作為 token 有幾項限制。

cues.en: Now, to be clear, these are not fatal flaws, but they are significant enough limitations that it motivates using subwords and words as tokens.
cues.zh: 說清楚一點，這些不是致命缺陷，但限制夠大，足以促使我們改用子詞與單字作為 token。

cues.en: One problem is that the International Unicode System recognizes over 150,000 characters, and this number
cues.zh: 其中一個問題是，國際 Unicode 系統收錄超過 15 萬個字元，而且這個數目

cues.en: is actually increasing over time because new characters get introduced or adapted.
cues.zh: 會隨著新字元的引進或採用而持續增加。

cues.en: And this would actually mean that the tokenization schemes would need to be changing over time, which
cues.zh: 這意味著斷詞方案也得隨時間改變，

cues.en: would also mean that the large language models would need to be retrained, or at least fine tuned each time the tokenization scheme is updated.
cues.zh: 每次更新斷詞方案，大型語言模型就得重新訓練，至少也需要微調。

cues.en: That is technically possible, but just not really feasible economically.
cues.zh: 技術上辦得到，但在經濟上並不實際。

cues.en: A second problem is that a purely character based tokenization scheme completely ignores the statistical
cues.zh: 第二個問題是，純字元斷詞方案完全忽略了

cues.en: regularities that are present in languages, and those statistical regularities can actually be leveraged to understand and produce text.
cues.zh: 語言中存在的統計規律，而這些規律其實可用來理解及產生文字。

cues.en: For example, in English, an H is more likely to follow a W or a T compared to, for example, a Q or an x.
cues.zh: 例如英文的 H 接在 W 或 T 後面的機率，比接在 Q 或 X 後面高。

cues.en: So this is meaningful information, and a character based tokenization scheme would make that kind of information just much harder for a language model to learn.
cues.zh: 這是有意義的資訊，但若採用字元斷詞，語言模型就更難學到這類資訊。

cues.en: The third problem is that a character based tokenization scheme just requires a lot more memory, because most words have many characters in them.
cues.zh: 第三個問題是，字元斷詞需要更多記憶體，因為大多數單字包含多個字元。

cues.en: Now, you saw that already in the previous slide with the word hello.
cues.zh: 上一張投影片的 hello 例子已經說明了這點。

cues.en: And the issue here is that language models have limited context windows that they can process.
cues.zh: 這裡的問題在於，語言模型能處理的上下文視窗有限。

cues.en: I will get much more into these kinds of details later on in the course, but the context window is
cues.zh: 稍後課程會更深入談這些細節。不過，上下文視窗

cues.en: basically how far back in the text the model can actually process information.
cues.zh: 基本上就是模型能回頭處理多長的文字資訊。

cues.en: So imagine that a model has a context window of 1000 tokens, and if each token is a character, then
cues.zh: 假設模型的上下文視窗是 1,000 個 token，而每個 token 都是一個字元，

cues.en: a thousand tokens is maybe around 200 words, which is basically just one paragraph.
cues.zh: 那麼 1,000 個 token 可能只有大約 200 個單字，基本上就一段文字。

cues.en: In contrast, a subword or word based tokenization system would mean that a thousand tokens is maybe
cues.zh: 相較之下，若採子詞或單字斷詞，1,000 個 token 可能

cues.en: 800 words, which is, let's say, four times as much information in the text that the language model can use to classify documents or generate new text.
cues.zh: 相當於 800 個單字。也就是說，語言模型可用來分類文件或產生新文字的資訊，大約多了四倍。

cues.en: Anyway, the conclusion from this slide is that a purely character based tokenization scheme is theoretically
cues.zh: 總之，這張投影片的結論是，純字元斷詞在理論上

cues.en: possible, but it just has a number of limitations that motivate using subwords and words.
cues.zh: 可行，但有一些限制，因此促使我們使用子詞與單字。

cues.en: Okay, there's a neat website that you can use to explore tokenization, so let's go check that out.
cues.zh: 有個很棒的網站，可以用來探索斷詞。我們來看看。

cues.en: So let's start just by typing in.
cues.zh: 先直接輸入

cues.en: Hello.
cues.zh: hello。

cues.en: So what we see here is the word hello has one token.
cues.zh: 這裡可以看到，hello 這個字只有一個 token。

cues.en: And that token corresponds to the token index or the integer 1533.
cues.zh: 這個 token 對應的索引，也就是整數，是 1533

cues.en: Nine.
Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: So that is the token that ChatGPT four uses to encode the word hello.
cues.zh: 這就是 ChatGPT-4 用來編碼 hello 的 token。

cues.en: Now here's something interesting I'm going to again use hello.
cues.zh: 有趣的是，我再輸入一次 hello，

cues.en: But put a space in front of it.
cues.zh: 不過在前面加上一個空白。

cues.en: And now you can see there's a space here.
cues.zh: 現在可以看到這裡有個空白。

cues.en: We still have only one token.
cues.zh: 依然只有一個 token。

cues.en: So there's one token for hello with a space in front of it.
cues.zh: 也就是說，前面帶空白的 hello 也是一個 token。

cues.en: And that's actually a different number.
cues.zh: 但它的編號不同。

cues.en: This is now 24,000 something.
cues.zh: 現在是兩萬四千多。

cues.en: So notice you can keep your eyes focused on this number over here.
cues.zh: 請盯著這裡的數字看。

cues.en: When I get rid of this space here it becomes a different token.
cues.zh: 我移除這個空白後，它就變成另一個 token。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: Now let's write some text.
cues.zh: 現在來寫一段文字。

cues.en: Hello.
cues.zh: 你好。

cues.en: My name is Mike, and I like to drink.
cues.zh: 我叫 Mike，我喜歡喝，

cues.en: I like to drink sparkling water because I find it refreshing.
cues.zh: 我喜歡喝氣泡水，因為覺得很清爽。

cues.en: Okay, so here you see the different colors correspond to the different tokens.
cues.zh: 可以看到，不同顏色對應不同 token。

cues.en: And a lot of these tokens correspond to entire words again with spaces in front of them.
cues.zh: 其中很多 token 都對應完整的單字，同樣包含前面的空白。

cues.en: You can see this little dot here in front of it.
cues.zh: 你可以看到前面這個小點。

cues.en: And in this example you can see that every individual word corresponds to a unique token, so we haven't broken up any words into separate tokens.
cues.zh: 這個例子裡，每個單字都對應各自的 token，所以沒有單字被拆成多個 token。

cues.en: Let's check out a different tokenizer.
cues.zh: 換個 tokenizer 看看。

cues.en: I'm actually going to copy this and then go down to.
cues.zh: 我先複製這段文字，然後往下找到，

cues.en: Let's do the tokenizer for.
cues.zh: 我們來用這個 tokenizer，

cues.en: I'm looking for.
cues.zh: 我在找，

cues.en: Let's do llama here.
cues.zh: 就用 Llama 吧。

cues.en: Okay so this is pretty interesting.
cues.zh: 這很有意思。

cues.en: We have exactly the same text over here.
cues.zh: 這裡的文字完全相同。

cues.en: And now with a different tokenizer we have some words correspond to single tokens.
cues.zh: 但換成另一個 tokenizer 後，有些單字對應單一 token，

cues.en: And also some words are broken up into sub words like this.
cues.zh: 有些單字則被拆成這樣的子詞。

cues.en: Refreshing is actually three tokens.
cues.zh: refreshing 實際上有三個 token。

cues.en: We have ref resh and hing or rez and hing.
cues.zh: 分成 ref、resh 和 hing，或者說 rez 和 hing。

cues.en: So different tokenizer and sparkling is also broken up.
cues.zh: tokenizer 不同，sparkling 也被拆開了。

cues.en: So different tokenizers that correspond to different language models actually break up text in different ways.
cues.zh: 所以，不同語言模型所對應的 tokenizer，拆分文字的方式也不同。

cues.en: You're going to learn a lot more about how these tokens are actually created and what implications this
cues.zh: 關於這些 token 如何產生，以及這對大型語言模型

cues.en: has for processing text in large language models.
cues.zh: 處理文字有何影響，你還會學到更多。

cues.en: That comes later on in this section and later in the course.
cues.zh: 這一章後面，以及課程稍後，都會談到。

cues.en: Now that I've introduced you to the idea and importance of tokens, you might be expecting me to say that llms work on tokens.
cues.zh: 介紹過 token 的概念與重要性之後，你可能以為我會說 LLM 處理的是 token。

cues.en: Well, if you expected that, then you might be surprised at the answer is actually no.
cues.zh: 如果你這樣想，可能會意外：答案其實是否定的。

cues.en: Language models do not actually process or even see the tokens.
cues.zh: 語言模型實際上不會處理，甚至不會看到 token 本身。

cues.en: The tokens, in fact, are just an intervening step.
cues.zh: token 其實只是中間步驟。

cues.en: Instead, language models actually work with something called embeddings.
cues.zh: 語言模型真正處理的，是稱為嵌入的東西。

cues.en: So we have to translate text into tokens which are integers using a tokenization procedure.
cues.zh: 所以，必須先透過斷詞程序，把文字轉成整數編號的 token，

cues.en: And then we have to get from tokens to embeddings.
cues.zh: 再從 token 轉換成嵌入。

cues.en: And then the language models actually work with the embeddings.
cues.zh: 接著，語言模型實際處理嵌入。

cues.en: In fact, language models are entirely about token embeddings.
cues.zh: 事實上，語言模型的運作全都圍繞 token 嵌入。

cues.en: That's literally the unit of processing throughout the entire language model.
cues.zh: 它就是整個語言模型的處理單位。

cues.en: So let me give you a quick overview of what that looks like.
cues.zh: 讓我簡單說明整個流程。

cues.en: We start with text that is human readable.
cues.zh: 一開始是人類能讀懂的文字。

cues.en: This is an Amazon review or a book section or a chat message that you've written in the text field of a ChatGPT.
cues.zh: 例如 Amazon 評論、書中的一節，或你在 ChatGPT 輸入欄中寫的訊息。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: Then that text is converted into tokens, which is then converted into indices, and then they are translated
cues.zh: 文字先轉成 token，再轉成索引，接著轉成

cues.en: into embeddings.
cues.zh: 嵌入。

cues.en: I'm going to define what embeddings are in the next slide.
cues.zh: 下一張投影片會定義嵌入。

cues.en: And there's a whole section of the course just on embeddings.
cues.zh: 而且，課程有一整章專門談嵌入。

cues.en: But suffice it to say that they are a vectorized and dense representation of token indices.
cues.zh: 目前先知道，它是 token 索引的一種向量化、稠密表示即可。

cues.en: Anyway, so the embedding then go through what's called an unembedding matrix, which back transforms
cues.zh: 接著，嵌入會經過所謂的反嵌入矩陣，

cues.en: the embeddings representation back into tokens, which is then converted back into text.
cues.zh: 把嵌入表示轉回 token，再轉回文字。

cues.en: Of course, the key to transformers and successful modern language models is the attention mechanism.
cues.zh: 當然，Transformer 與成功的現代語言模型，其關鍵是注意力機制。

cues.en: Now, I'm not going to talk about this mechanism until later on in the course, but basically all of
cues.zh: 這個機制要到課程後面才會說明，不過基本上，

cues.en: this fancy attention stuff is just making like minor tweaks and modifications to the embeddings.
cues.zh: 這些複雜的注意力運作，就是對嵌入進行細微調整與修改。

cues.en: So this is basically the flow of a language model.
cues.zh: 這大致就是語言模型的流程。

cues.en: And the point is that the real action in a language model is not happening to the text, and is not happening to the integer token IDs.
cues.zh: 重點在於，語言模型的實際運算，不是作用在文字，也不是作用在整數形式的 token ID 上。

cues.en: Instead, everything is acting on the embeddings and processing and modifying the embeddings between
cues.zh: 所有運算都作用在嵌入上，對嵌入進行處理與修改，從

cues.en: when they are transformed from tokens to when they are transformed back into tokens and then ultimately back into text.
cues.zh: 它由 token 轉成嵌入，直到再轉回 token、最後轉回文字為止。

cues.en: So yeah, embeddings are a big deal.
cues.zh: 所以，嵌入非常重要。

cues.en: Now, I'm sure you're wondering what these mysterious embeddings actually are.
cues.zh: 你一定想知道，這些神祕的嵌入到底是什麼。

cues.en: An embedding is a dense numeric representation of a token.
cues.zh: 嵌入就是 token 的稠密數值表示。

cues.en: Embeddings are actually much better than tokens because they can represent more information, using
cues.zh: 嵌入比 token 好得多，因為能用

cues.en: fewer numbers, and also information that allows for semantic relationships to be expressed across different tokens.
cues.zh: 更少的數字表達更多資訊，也能呈現不同 token 之間的語意關係。

cues.en: For example, let's take the two words Spain and France.
cues.zh: 例如，看看 Spain 和 France 這兩個字。

cues.en: These are represented by different integers, and those two integers have absolutely nothing whatsoever to do with each other.
cues.zh: 它們以不同整數表示，但這兩個整數彼此毫無關係。

cues.en: It's just two random numbers.
cues.zh: 只是兩個隨機數字。

cues.en: But the embeddings for France and for Spain are going to show some interesting patterns of correlations,
cues.zh: 然而，France 與 Spain 的嵌入會呈現有趣的相關模式，

cues.en: because those two words actually represent things that are meaningfully related to each other.
cues.zh: 因為這兩個字所代表的事物，彼此有意義上的關聯。

cues.en: Now tokens.
cues.zh: 但 token，

cues.en: Token indices cannot handle that kind of relationship.
cues.zh: 也就是 token 索引，無法處理這種關係。

cues.en: But embeddings actually do encode these sorts of relationships and allow for the language models to
cues.zh: 嵌入則能將這類關係編碼，讓語言模型

cues.en: modify and shape these relationships in context specific and dynamic ways.
cues.zh: 依照特定上下文，以動態方式調整、塑造這些關係。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: This might seem all very opaque and difficult to understand.
cues.zh: 這些可能聽起來很抽象、難以理解。

cues.en: Let's have a simple example.
cues.zh: 我們來看個簡單例子。

cues.en: Here you see a two dimensional plane.
cues.zh: 這裡是一個二維平面。

cues.en: So the two dimensions are size and friendliness.
cues.zh: 兩個維度是體型與友善程度。

cues.en: And I'm going to plot several different animals on this graph according to these two attributes.
cues.zh: 我會依照這兩種屬性，把幾種動物畫在圖上。

cues.en: So let's start with a dog.
cues.zh: 先從狗開始。

cues.en: A dog is not huge, but kind of big and very friendly.
cues.zh: 狗不算巨大，但有點大，而且非常友善。

cues.en: Most of the time.
cues.zh: 大多數時候是如此。

cues.en: So I'm going to put dog up here.
cues.zh: 所以，我把狗放在這裡。

cues.en: Next we have a cat.
cues.zh: 接著是貓。

cues.en: Cats are a little bit smaller than dogs, and let's say a little bit less friendly than dogs, at least on average.
cues.zh: 貓比狗小一點，至少平均而言，也比狗沒那麼友善。

cues.en: Of course, I mean, no offense to the cat lovers in the audience.
cues.zh: 當然，我無意冒犯喜歡貓的各位。

cues.en: This is just a simple example to illustrate the concept of an embedding.
cues.zh: 這只是用來說明嵌入概念的簡單例子。

cues.en: Okay, that said, I think we can all agree on the positions of some of these other animals.
cues.zh: 不過，接下來幾種動物的位置，大家應該都同意。

cues.en: Mosquitoes are small and unfriendly.
cues.zh: 蚊子很小，也不友善。

cues.en: Hippos are huge and extremely unfriendly.
cues.zh: 河馬很大，而且極不友善。

cues.en: And ladybugs are also pretty small, though not as small as a mosquito.
cues.zh: 瓢蟲也很小，但沒有蚊子那麼小。

cues.en: And I guess they're pretty friendly.
cues.zh: 我想，牠們算滿友善的。

cues.en: Okay, so now we have a two dimensional embedding space, and we can assign a coordinate to each of
cues.zh: 現在有了一個二維嵌入空間，我們可以依照各種動物

cues.en: these animals according to where they are on these two axes.
cues.zh: 在這兩條軸上的位置，替牠們指定座標。

cues.en: For example, let's represent dog using the numbers 0.5 and 0.9.
cues.zh: 例如，用 0.5 和 0.9 表示狗。

cues.en: So let's say 0.5 on the size axis and 0.9 on the friendliness axis.
cues.zh: 也就是體型軸上為 0.5，友善程度軸上為 0.9。

cues.en: And now for cats I'm going to say 0.4 and 0.7.
cues.zh: 至於貓，我設成 0.4 和 0.7。

cues.en: And here are the other animals.
cues.zh: 其他動物則是這些值。

cues.en: So what have we done here.
cues.zh: 我們做了什麼？

cues.en: We have taken five completely different words that have completely different and arbitrary integers, and transformed them into two numbers.
cues.zh: 把五個完全不同、整數編號也任意且毫不相關的單字，轉成各自的兩個數值。

cues.en: That allows for meaningful comparisons across the different words.
cues.zh: 這讓不同單字之間可以進行有意義的比較，

cues.en: Or, you know, the things in the real world that these words are referencing.
cues.zh: 也就是比較這些字在現實世界中所指涉的事物。

cues.en: So this is called a dense representation.
cues.zh: 這稱為稠密表示。

cues.en: And this right here would be called an embedding vector.
cues.zh: 而這裡稱為嵌入向量。

cues.en: So this is the embedding vector for the word dog the embedding vector for the word cat.
cues.zh: 這是 dog 的嵌入向量，這是 cat 的嵌入向量。

cues.en: And this will be called the embedding space.
cues.zh: 整個空間則稱為嵌入空間。

cues.en: Now this is just a little toy example to help you with the concept of an embedding space.
cues.zh: 這只是個小型示例，幫助你理解嵌入空間的概念。

cues.en: In practice, embeddings are high dimensional.
cues.zh: 實務上的嵌入是高維的。

cues.en: This graph shows two dimensions, but the embedding spaces that we will be working with here in this course are around 1000 dimensional.
cues.zh: 這張圖只有兩個維度，但本課程使用的嵌入空間大約有 1,000 個維度。

cues.en: It varies depending on the language model, but somewhere around 1000 dimensions.
cues.zh: 維度數依語言模型而異，不過大致在 1,000 左右。

cues.en: And the modern frontier models like GPT and Claude and Gemini and Deep, they can have several thousand dimensions compared to these two over here.
cues.zh: 而 GPT、Claude、Gemini 和 Deep 這類現代前沿模型，嵌入可能有數千維，而不是這裡的兩維。

cues.en: Secondly, I just made up these two axes to be understandable to us.
cues.zh: 第二點，這兩條軸是我為了方便理解而自行設定的。

cues.en: But the real embeddings are generally not human interpretable.
cues.zh: 實際的嵌入通常無法人類直觀解讀。

cues.en: We will explore this later on in the course, and you will see that there are cases where we can define
cues.zh: 課程後面會進一步探索，你會看到有些情況下，我們能在

cues.en: directions in this high dimensional embedding space that are human interpretable, but they're tricky to find.
cues.zh: 高維嵌入空間中，找出人類可以解讀的方向，但很難找到。

cues.en: They're not very reliable.
cues.zh: 這些方向也不太可靠。

cues.en: And those are really more the exception than the rule.
cues.zh: 而且，這比較像例外，並非常態。

cues.en: So in general, the real embedding vectors are not human interpretable.
cues.zh: 所以，一般而言，人類無法直接解讀實際的嵌入向量。

cues.en: Third point is, the vectors themselves are not fixed, but instead are dynamically modified as the language model processes text.
cues.zh: 第三點，向量本身不是固定的，而會隨語言模型處理文字而動態改變。

cues.en: For example, if you're chatting with ChatGPT about a Chihuahua and then you use the word dog internally,
cues.zh: 例如，你和 ChatGPT 聊吉娃娃，接著使用 dog 這個字，

cues.en: ChatGPT will actually modify these numbers here so that the 0.5 might get converted to like a 0.1, for example.
cues.zh: ChatGPT 內部就會修改這些數字，例如將 0.5 改成 0.1。

cues.en: And maybe you're talking about a cartoon where a hippo is cute and friendly and grants magical wishes,
cues.zh: 又或者，你在談一部卡通，裡面的河馬可愛、友善，還能施展魔法實現願望，

cues.en: and then this minus one over here on the friendliness axis might get bumped up to 0.8.
cues.zh: 那麼友善程度軸上的負 1，可能就會提高到 0.8。

cues.en: Okay, so I hope this slide makes conceptual sense.
cues.zh: 希望這張投影片能幫你理解概念。

cues.zh: 關於嵌入，課程後面還有很多內容。

cues.en: For now, I want to discuss a little bit about why tokenization is difficult.
cues.zh: 現在先稍微談談，為什麼斷詞很困難。

cues.en: On the one hand, if we have a tokenization scheme with relatively few tokens, then this is actually
cues.zh: 一方面，如果斷詞方案的 token 數量較少，

cues.en: good because it reduces the amount of memory required to learn and process tokens.
cues.zh: 好處是能減少學習與處理 token 所需的記憶體。

cues.en: And it's also good for dealing with infrequent words.
cues.zh: 這也有利於處理少見的單字，

cues.en: Generalizing to new contexts and new words.
cues.zh: 並泛化到新的上下文與新單字。

cues.en: But it's also less efficient.
cues.zh: 不過，效率也較差。

cues.en: It doesn't learn long range dependencies very well, and in general, models that use character based
cues.zh: 它不太擅長學習長距離依賴，而且一般而言，採用字元斷詞的

cues.en: tokenization schemes are just not going to sound very human like.
cues.zh: 模型，說話不會那麼像人類。

cues.en: On the other hand, having more tokens generally increases text compression, which means you can pack more information over longer documents more effectively.
cues.zh: 另一方面，較多的 token 通常能提高文字壓縮率，讓較長文件中的更多資訊能更有效地放入模型。

cues.en: That's all good.
cues.zh: 這些都是好處。

cues.en: That's a good thing.
cues.zh: 這是件好事。

cues.en: But it also requires even larger data sets and more computation time for training.
cues.zh: 但訓練時也需要更大的資料集與更多計算時間。

cues.en: So tokenization is learned from statistical dependencies in training text, and those dependencies change across languages.
cues.zh: 斷詞是從訓練文字的統計依賴關係中學得，而不同語言的依賴關係會改變。

cues.en: They also change within a language in different types of text.
cues.zh: 即使在同一語言中，不同類型的文字也有所不同。

cues.en: So for example, a tokenizer based on Twitter messages or whatever that, uh, website and app is now
cues.zh: 例如，以 Twitter 訊息為基礎的 tokenizer，無論那個網站和應用程式現在

cues.en: called uh tokenizer based on tweets will be different from a tokenizer based on scientific publications in medical journals.
cues.zh: 叫什麼，以推文為基礎的 tokenizer，會和以醫學期刊的科學論文為基礎的 tokenizer 不同。

cues.en: Just because the nature of the writing is different in those two data sets.
cues.zh: 因為這兩種資料集的寫作性質不同。

cues.en: And this also means that the tokenization procedure is more difficult in languages where there is less text available for training.
cues.zh: 這也表示，可用來訓練的文字較少時，該語言的斷詞程序會更困難。

cues.en: Also, different companies that make tokenizers can use different training protocols or different criteria based on different goals.
cues.zh: 此外，不同的 tokenizer 開發公司，可能依照不同目標，採取不同訓練流程或準則。

cues.en: So, for example, if your primary goal for a language model is generating new text like a chat model,
cues.zh: 例如，如果語言模型的主要目的是產生新文字，像聊天模型、

cues.en: a chatbot versus classifying existing text, then that actually leads to different tokenization methods.
cues.zh: 聊天機器人，而不是分類既有文字，就會採用不同的斷詞方法。

cues.en: And you'll see some examples of this later in this section.
cues.zh: 這一章稍後會看到一些例子。

cues.en: But what does all this stuff actually mean?
cues.zh: 不過，這些事情到底代表什麼？

cues.en: Are there actually implications of this, or does it not matter how a language is tokenized?
cues.zh: 真的有影響嗎？還是語言如何斷詞其實無關緊要？

cues.en: It turns out that this actually is pretty meaningful.
cues.zh: 其實影響很大。

cues.en: Tokenization is not so straightforward, and it depends on several assumptions.
cues.zh: 斷詞並不簡單，而且依賴幾項假設。

cues.en: You have to make decisions about how to tokenize, and that's only the first step.
cues.zh: 你得決定如何斷詞，而這只是第一步。

cues.zh: 斷詞後建立嵌入矩陣，還需要更多訓練，以及更多選擇、

cues.en: and decisions and parameters, including the fact that the training data is really crucial for creating and tokenizing Organizing and creating the embedding matrices.
cues.zh: 決策和參數。尤其訓練資料，對斷詞的建立、整理與嵌入矩陣的建立都非常關鍵。

cues.en: Now, as I already mentioned, different data sets will give different results, and that can have a pretty significant implication for the performance of the language model.
cues.zh: 如前所述，不同資料集會產生不同結果，而這可能顯著影響語言模型的效能。

cues.zh: 所以，這些事情相當有挑戰性。

cues.zh: 而且，這些全都發生在語言模型看到第一筆資料之前。

cues.zh: 因此，確實令人望而生畏。

cues.zh: 這支影片想傳達的是，雖然將單字轉成
